welcome.summary: A catalogue of components and foundations for building consistent, accessible and verifiable experiences.

steps.title: 1. Start with the foundations
steps.text: Check colour, typography, spacing, radius and icons before deciding how a piece should look.

steps.title: 2. Look up the component
steps.text: Each component gathers its states, variants, accessibility and runnable examples.

steps.title: 3. Report a gap
steps.text: If a case is not documented, do not improvise API, token, variant or behaviour.

docs.summary: Provides an icon from the Nephos core with consistent size, family and accessibility, without introducing colour or artwork outside the approved set.
docs.sizeCaption: The approved sizes, with real nph-icon instances.
docs.derivedText1: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: design.md for the technical contract and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for decisions P01, P02, P03, P17, P19, P20 and P21. The nph-icon spec sheet and the DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file complete the component contract. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: A control or piece of content needs an icon that exists in the Nephos core.
The icon reinforces a label, state or direction without replacing the textual information.
whenNotToUse: The action is domain-specific or has consequences: use a text label alongside the icon.
The requested icon does not exist in the core: report the gap and wait for a decision.
api: Required, in kebab-case and limited to the {total} icons of the Nephos core.
regular by default; solid when the context needs more visual presence. Both exist for every name in the core.
sm, md or lg; free values are not accepted.
Absent or empty makes the icon decorative and applies aria-hidden. A non-empty value provides its accessible name.
Takes no focus, click or touch; the surrounding control defines the interaction.
Exposes no colour property and no initial ::part; inherits currentColor from the context.
docs.coreText: The set is Font Awesome Pro and Classic is the default family. The full catalogue, with search, is under Icons Overview, in this same folder.
docs.coreRule: regular and solid exist for every name in the core; regular is the default, and solid comes in when the context needs more visual presence. Never invent artwork outside the collection. Light, Thin and Sharp are forbidden. Duotone is allowed only in structural navigation, without mixing families within one group, and has no artwork available yet.
docs.sizeText: Size is not a visual variant: it comes from a semantic token, and free values do not exist. The box is always square; the artwork is centred and scaled by height.
sizeTable: Inside a control, a table cell, a field, and next to 14px text. When in doubt, this is the one.
Menu item, tab and highlighted action, where sm looks small next to the label. Do not use inside an ordinary button.
Section heading, empty state, and an icon that carries meaning on its own. Do not use in dense screens or in lists.
docs.sizeOverflow: eye, eye-slash and star are 18 wide by nature, above the 16 of the box: the box normalises height and alignment, not width. The artwork overflows centred, without clipping and without rescaling.
docs.colorText: Colour is inherited from the context through currentColor. There is no icon colour token, and colour is not a property of the component. The gap to the text is space/inline-tight and belongs to the container that composes icon and text, not to the icon.
accessibility: With visible text beside it, the icon is decorative and takes aria-hidden — otherwise the screen reader reads it twice.
With no visible text, aria-label is required.
A meaningful icon requires 3:1 contrast (WCAG 1.4.11).
The icon is not the touch target: the target is the surrounding control, with control/height-large on touch screens.
An isolated icon takes no focus; the surrounding control defines keyboard behaviour.
Icon and colour are never the only signal of state or action.
docs.invalidText: A name outside the core, a missing size or one outside the approved list, or a variant that does not exist render no icon and fail development validation. There is no visual fallback and no free size. The error is reported through console.error in development only.
docs.invalidPointer: The cases are demonstrated under Validation › Invalid input.
antiPatterns: Do not use an icon alone to delete, approve, publish, export or perform any other domain-specific action.
Do not put the Font Awesome Pro package, files or secret into versioned material.
Do not create a visual variant just to fill a matrix.
Do not use Duotone outside structural navigation, and do not mix Duotone and Classic in the same group.
Do not use a name outside the Nephos icon core.
Do not define colour as a property; the icon inherits currentColor from the context.

validation.variantsNote: regular and solid exist for every name in the core.
validation.sizesSummary: Size comes from a semantic token. There is no free value.
validation.sizesNote: The box normalises height and alignment, not width: eye, eye-slash and star overflow centred, without clipping and without rescaling.
validation.colorNote: None of the icons below was painted. They all inherit the colour of the context.
validation.a11ySummary: Decorative beside text; named when it stands alone.
validation.a11yDecorativeNote: Without label: aria-hidden on the host. The screen reader reads the text only once.
validation.a11yNamedNote: With label: role="img" and aria-label on the host. Only for a universal, recurring symbol; an action with consequences never stands alone.
validation.a11yFocusNote: The icon never takes focus: keyboard and touch target belong to the surrounding control.
validation.invalidIntro: The four cases below draw nothing and take up no space. Open the console to see one error per invalid property.
invalidCases: a variant that does not exist
a free size does not exist

badgeDocs.summary: A short tag that labels the status or the category of an item. If there is nothing to write, there is no badge.
badgeDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-badge spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P68. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: To label the status or the category of an item.
Choose the severity by meaning. A permanent status uses secondary or primary; success confirms an event that has just happened.
Turn the icon on only to reinforce the word.
whenNotToUse: As a button: the badge takes no click and no focus. Use nph-button.
success as a permanent badge: use secondary or primary.
A badge without text, with only an icon.
Two status badges on the same item.
A sentence inside the badge: supporting text stays outside the component.
api: The severity, by meaning: primary (default), secondary, info, warn, help, danger or success. Reflected to the attribute.
The emphasis: solid (default) or light. Reflected to the attribute.
One or two words, already localized. It is the accessible name. Empty or only spaces: there is no badge.
A name from the nph-icon core, before the text. Empty: no icon.
badgeDocs.variantsCaption: The severities in the solid and light emphases; in the second row of each emphasis, with an icon.
anatomy: radius/full; space/inline-tight on top and bottom and space/control-padding on the sides. The background colour comes from the severity and the emphasis.
Before the text, at icon/size-sm, in the text colour, space/inline-tight away from it. Artwork from nph-icon.
text/label-sm, on a single line. It is the accessible name of the component.
accessibility: Contrast
The text passes 4.5:1 in every severity and emphasis, in both modes and in every brand; the lowest value is 4.64:1, in primary light in light mode.
Visible focus
The badge takes no click and no focus. For an action, use nph-button.
Colour is not the only signal
Every badge has text: colour is never the only signal, and the icon only reinforces the word.
Touch target
It is not a touch target: the badge takes no click.
Accessible name
The text is the accessible name of the component. The icon is decorative.
badgeDocs.exampleIcon: Status with an icon reinforcing the word.
antiPatterns: Using it as a button: the badge takes no click and no focus. Use nph-button.
Using success as a permanent badge: use secondary or primary.
A badge without text, with only an icon.
Two status badges on the same item.
A sentence inside the badge: supporting text stays outside the component.
Painting the background or the text by hand: the colour comes from the severity and the emphasis.

buttonDocs.summary: Triggers an action identified by text. It varies in severity, emphasis, size and state, with an optional icon at the start or the end. Without text, it is the icon-only button.
buttonDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-button spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P68. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: To start an action identified by text, such as save or send.
Write in the text what happens on click.
Choose the severity by the meaning of the action, never by colour.
Choose the emphasis by how much the action stands out: solid, outline, light or ghost.
Use size large on touch screens.
Without text, use the icon-only button and give it an accessible name.
whenNotToUse: To show a field error: validation belongs to the field (nph-field).
Icon only on an action with consequences, such as delete or publish.
size compact as the main target on a touch screen.
api: The severity, by the meaning of the action: primary (default), secondary, info, warn, help, danger or success. Reflected to the attribute.
How much the action stands out: solid (default), outline, light or ghost. outline, light and ghost exist only in primary, secondary and danger. Reflected to the attribute.
compact, default (the default) or large. large meets the 44 px touch target. Reflected to the attribute.
What happens on click, already localized. It is the accessible name.
A name from the nph-icon core before the text, at icon/size-sm. It can coexist with icon-end.
A name from the nph-icon core after the text, at icon/size-sm.
Accessible name of the button without text. Required there; with text, it is not used.
Turns the button off: it leaves the Tab order and fires no click. Reflected to the attribute.
Shows the nph-spinner in place of the start icon; the text stays, focus remains and the click does not reach the consumer. Reflected to the attribute.
buttonDocs.variantsCaption: The severities in each emphasis, at the default size. Hover to see the hover state and use Tab to see focus.
buttonDocs.sizesText: The height comes from control/height-compact, -default or -large. The text is text/label-md in all of them. Without text, the button is square and the icon follows the box: sm in compact, md in default and lg in large.
buttonDocs.sizesCaption: compact, default and large, with text, with an icon and icon only.
states: Rest. The colour conveys the severity of the action.
The surface changes to the hover token of the severity and emphasis.
For keyboard users: a border in the severity colour and a halo outside it, without changing the size. In secondary, the border is focus/border.
The whole button at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order.
The nph-spinner in place of the start icon. The text stays.
accessibility: Contrast
Text and icon pass 4.5:1 in every severity and emphasis, in both modes and in every brand; the lowest value is 4.64:1, in primary outline and light in light mode. Borders pass 3:1.
Visible focus
On focus, the border and the halo appear for keyboard users.
Colour is not the only signal
Colour is never the only signal of intent, focus or state: the text says what happens on click.
Touch target
size large meets the 44 px touch target; compact is not a main target on a touch screen.
Accessible name
The text is the name of the button. Without text, the name comes from label, which is required.
Keyboard
Tab moves in and out; Enter and Space activate.
buttonDocs.exampleConsequence: An action with consequences, always with text.
buttonDocs.exampleIconOnly: A universal action without text, with an accessible name.
antiPatterns: Showing a field error on the button: validation belongs to the field (nph-field).
Using icon only on an action with consequences, such as delete or publish.
Enlarging the icon to add emphasis.
Using colour as the only signal of intent, focus or state.
Navigating to another destination with the button.
Creating a severity, emphasis or size outside the matrix, or painting the button by hand.
